questions.question_text:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Period } (n) & 0.5\% & 0.6\% \\ \hline 180 & 118.5035 & 109.8845 \\ 240 & 139.5808 & 127.0084 \\ \hline \end{array}$
A buyer can afford repayments of $\$1800$ at the end of each month on a home loan at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($0.5\%$ per month).
Use the present value table above to find how much more they can borrow by extending the term from $15$ years ($180$ months) to $20$ years ($240$ months), to the nearest dollar.

options.why: Reported the borrowing capacity for $240$ months instead of the increase.
Reported the borrowing capacity for $180$ months instead of the increase.

questions.solution_text:
$r = 6\% \div 12 = 0.5\%$
The two terms contain $180$ and $240$ end-of-month repayments of the same amount.
$PV_{15} = 1800 \times 118.5035 = \$213\,306.30$
$PV_{20} = 1800 \times 139.5808 = \$251\,245.44$
$\text{Increase} = 251\,245.44 - 213\,306.30 = \$37\,939.14$
$= \$37\,939$ to the nearest dollar.
The longer term increases borrowing capacity; subtract before rounding.

questions.question_text:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Years} & 1\% & 2\% & 3\% & 4\% \\ \hline 4 & 4.060 & 4.122 & 4.184 & 4.246 \\ 5 & 5.101 & 5.204 & 5.309 & 5.416 \\ 6 & 6.152 & 6.308 & 6.468 & 6.633 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Liam deposits $\$3000$ at the end of each year for $7$ years.
For the first $6$ years, interest is $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually. For the seventh year, the rate increases to $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Using the future value table above, calculate the balance at the end of the seventh year, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Added the final deposit to the six-year balance without adding interest for the seventh year.
Applied the final year's $5\%$ interest but omitted the seventh deposit of $\$3000$.
Used $4\%$ interest in the seventh year instead of the new $5\%$ rate.

questions.solution_text:
The first $6$ end-of-year deposits use $r = 4\%$, $n = 6$ and factor $6.633$.
$\text{Balance after 6 years} = 3000 \times 6.633 = \$19\,899.00$
$\text{Balance after 7 years} = 19\,899.00 \times 1.05 + 3000$
$= \$23\,893.95$
Only the existing balance earns seventh-year interest; the seventh deposit is added at year-end.

questions.question_text:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Period } (n) & 0.5\% & 0.6\% \\ \hline 180 & 118.5035 & 109.8845 \\ 240 & 139.5808 & 127.0084 \\ \hline \end{array}$
A buyer purchases a property for $\$330\,000$ and pays a cash deposit of $\$50\,000$ immediately.
The remaining amount is borrowed at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($0.5\%$ per month), with equal repayments at the end of each month over $20$ years ($240$ months).
Use the present value table above to calculate the monthly repayment, to the nearest dollar.

options.why: Used the full purchase price of $\$330\,000$ as the loan principal without deducting the deposit.
Added the deposit to the purchase price, using a principal of $\$380\,000$.
Used the $0.6\%$ factor $127.0084$ instead of the $0.5\%$ factor $139.5808$.

questions.solution_text:
The deposit is paid immediately, so only the remaining purchase price is borrowed.
$\text{Principal} = 330\,000 - 50\,000 = \$280\,000$
$r = 6\% \div 12 = 0.5\%, n = 20 \times 12 = 240$
$M = \dfrac{280\,000}{139.5808}$
$= \$2006$ to the nearest dollar.
Use the $240$-period present value factor for end-of-month repayments; round the final repayment amount to the requested dollar.
